page.title: API tokens
page.subtitle: Let scripts and integrations call the Cellhive API as you, with only the access you choose.

warning.expired: Expired: requests with it are refused

mine.title: Your tokens
mine.intro: A token acts as you in this organization: it can never do more than you can, and only what its scopes allow.
mine.empty: You have no API tokens in this organization yet.
mine.disabled: API tokens are turned off for this organization: new tokens cannot be created and existing tokens do not work. Ask an organization admin.

all.title: Tokens of the organization
all.intro: Every member's tokens. Values are never shown; revoking stops a token immediately.

create.title: New API token
create.description: The token is shown once after you create it.
create.name: Name
create.accessHint: Start from a preset, then adjust. Writing does not include reading.

preset.readHint: Read records and the structure of tables.
preset.readWriteHint: Read, create, change and delete records.
preset.schemaHint: Create and change tables, fields and views; read records.
preset.automationHint: Read and change automations; read record values (previews, test sends, run details).
preset.mcpReadHint: For AI clients such as Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code: browse tables, query and summarize records.
preset.mcpReadWriteHint: Also create and update records: up to 50 per call, never deleting.

groups.recordsHint: Rows of your tables, files, import and export.
groups.schemaHint: Workspaces, bases, tables, fields and views.

create.noBases: You cannot open any base yet.
create.tooLong: Not allowed: this organization limits tokens to {{days}} days.
create.required: Not allowed: this organization requires tokens to expire.
create.noneWarning: A token that never expires keeps working until someone revokes it. Prefer an expiration and create a new token when it ends.

reveal.title: Copy your new token
reveal.warningTitle: This is the only time you can see it
reveal.warning: Cellhive stores only a fingerprint of the token. If you lose it, revoke it and create a new one.
reveal.label: Token
reveal.exampleHint: Send the token in the Authorization header. Keep it out of code repositories and logs.
reveal.confirm: I've saved the token somewhere safe
reveal.nag: Confirm that you've saved the token before closing.

revoke.title: Revoke “{{name}}”?
revoke.description: Integrations and scripts using this token stop working immediately. This cannot be undone.
revoke.descriptionOther: Integrations and scripts of {{owner}} using this token stop working immediately. This cannot be undone.

policy.title: Policy
policy.intro: Applies to every member of the organization.
policy.enabledHint: When off, no token can be created and every existing token stops working until you turn this on again. Tokens are not revoked.
policy.offWarning: Saving turns off every API token of the organization: integrations using them stop immediately.
policy.lifetimeInvalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to 3650.

policy.title: MCP clients
policy.intro: Members can connect AI clients such as Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code to Cellhive through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), with one of their API tokens. A client sees only what the token's owner can read, within the token's scopes and bases.
policy.enabledOff: Off: the MCP endpoint refuses every token.
policy.enabledOn: Members connect from “Connect via MCP” on their tokens. Every read of records is recorded in the audit log.
policy.writes: Let MCP clients create and update records
policy.writesHint: Only for tokens that can change records: up to 50 records per call, never deleting. Off: MCP clients only read.

allow_writes.on: MCP clients can now create and update records.
allow_writes.off: MCP clients can only read now.

enabled.title: Allow MCP clients?
enabled.lead: Members will be able to send the records they can read to the AI model that their MCP client uses.
enabled.point1: This holds even when the AI settings keep record values away from AI: those cover Cellhive's own AI provider, not the members' clients.
enabled.point2: A client acts as the token's owner: it never reads more than that person can, within the token's scopes and bases.
enabled.point3: Every read of records through MCP is recorded in the audit log, without the values.

allow_writes.title: Let MCP clients change records?
allow_writes.lead: Clients whose token can change records will be able to create and update records as the token's owner.
allow_writes.point1: Up to 50 records per call, with the owner's permissions; never deleting, never changing tables or fields. Automations run as for any API change.
allow_writes.point2: Records can hold text written by others, such as form submissions. A model may take it for instructions and write wrong data: keep clients asking before each change.
allow_writes.point3: A call sent again after a lost connection can create the same records twice.

connect.title: Connect via MCP
connect.description: Use “{{name}}” in an AI client that supports MCP.

hint.claudeCode: Run it in a terminal, then type /mcp in Claude Code to check the connection.
hint.cursor: Add it to ~/.cursor/mcp.json for every project, or to .cursor/mcp.json in one project.
hint.vscode: Add it to .vscode/mcp.json. VS Code asks for the token when it first starts the server and keeps it in its secret storage.

connect.placeholder: Replace {{masked}} with the full token. Cellhive showed it only once, when the token was created.
